deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page uses Riemann's normal form of the genus-3 (plane quartic) theory. It has 63 half-periods written as 3-bit characteristics (upper/lower rows such as 110/101). Six bitangents x, y, z, xi, eta, zeta are tied by three linear relations:
(R0) x+y+z+xi+eta+zeta=0
(R1) alpha x+beta y+gamma z+xi/alpha+eta/beta+zeta/gamma=0
(R2) alpha' x+beta' y+gamma' z+xi/alpha'+eta/beta'+zeta/gamma'=0
The quartic is sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0. A fourth set (alpha'', beta'', gamma'') comes from the linear dependence among these forms. A symbol (a b c) means the 3x3 determinant |1 1 1; a b c; a' b' c'|. The previous page asks when the bitangents of all pairs in a 'Gruppe' coincide. It lists degenerate cases: I (alpha beta gamma)=0; II alpha=beta; III; IV alpha=beta, alpha'=beta'; V alpha=...=gamma'=1. This page works out such special cases.

1. TOP BLOCK: a special value of alpha. The transcription reads 'alpha=0'; from the subtraction performed it is most likely alpha=1 (or alpha' = 1/alpha'). Then x and xi drop out of R1-R0 and R2-alpha' R0. This gives (my reconstruction) (beta-1)y+(gamma-1)z+(1/beta-1)eta+(1/gamma-1)zeta=0, and the analogous primed relation written on the page.

Riemann names four linear forms:
- a = eta+zeta
- b = beta y+gamma z
- c = y+z
- d = eta/beta+zeta/gamma

He forms the products a*b and c*d, i.e. the candidates sqrt((eta+zeta)(beta y+gamma z)) and sqrt((y+z)(eta/beta+zeta/gamma)). These are new pairs of lines whose product is a candidate 'bitangent pair'. He verifies:
- b - beta c = (gamma-beta) z
- b - gamma c = (beta-gamma) y
- a - beta d = (1-beta/gamma) zeta
- a - gamma d = (1-gamma/beta) eta

From these he forms the crossed pair:
- e = y+zeta, from (b - gamma c - gamma a + beta gamma d) = (beta-gamma) e
- f = eta/beta+gamma z, from gamma b - beta gamma c - a + gamma d

This gives the further candidate sqrt((y+zeta)(eta/beta+gamma z)). A fourth, sqrt((eta+z)(beta y+zeta/gamma)), is written without derivation.

He then looks for a pencil parameter lambda making suitable combinations work, via the conditions
-(1+lambda gamma)(lambda+gamma) = -gamma(1+lambda beta)(lambda+beta) = lambda(beta-gamma)^2.
Dividing by lambda gamma (respectively lambda beta gamma) turns these into
(lambda+1/lambda)+(gamma+1/gamma) = -(beta-gamma)^2/gamma
and
beta(lambda+1/lambda+beta+1/beta) = -(beta-gamma)^2/gamma.
Eliminating lambda+1/lambda gives a compatibility condition between beta and gamma. The right-margin lines are his attempts to simplify it: 2(gamma-beta)+1/gamma+beta^2/gamma-... and a claimed factor (1-1/(beta gamma))(beta-gamma)(beta/gamma-2).

2. SQUARE-ROOT RELATIONS. He writes two relations whose hypothesis is not stated on the page:
- sqrt((x+y+z)(xi+eta+zeta)) - sqrt(x xi) + sqrt(y eta) = 0
- sqrt((alpha x+beta y+gamma z)(xi/alpha+eta/beta+zeta/gamma)) - sqrt(alpha/beta x xi) + sqrt(beta/alpha y eta) = 0

Multiplying the first by sqrt(alpha/beta) and combining with the second eliminates sqrt(x xi). This leaves sqrt(alpha/beta) sqrt(A) ± sqrt(B) + (beta/alpha-1) sqrt(alpha/beta y eta) = 0, where A = (x+y+z)(xi+eta+zeta) and B = (alpha x+...)(xi/alpha+...). Squaring gives
2 sqrt(alpha/beta) sqrt(AB) = ±[(alpha/beta)A + B - (alpha/beta)(beta/alpha-1)^2 y eta],
which is the next displayed line.

3. BIT TABLES under 'alpha=beta'. These list, in characteristic notation, the bitangent pairs and groups affected in case II. They are the combinatorial bookkeeping for the '18 aehnliche Faelle'.

4. CASE alpha=beta, derivation of the second condition. Suppose a linear relation with multipliers lambda, lambda', lambda'' holds, with componentwise coefficients
- 1+alpha lambda+alpha' lambda' = alpha'' lambda''
- 1+beta lambda+beta' lambda' = beta'' lambda''
- the same with reciprocals.

Using alpha=beta and subtracting:
- (alpha'-beta')lambda' = (alpha''-beta'')lambda''
- (1/alpha'-1/beta')lambda' = (1/alpha''-1/beta'')lambda''

Dividing, since (u-v)/(1/u-1/v) = -uv, gives alpha' beta' = alpha'' beta''. This is the companion condition of case II. The marginal first line, (alpha'+1/alpha')-(beta'+1/beta')+(alpha'/alpha+alpha/alpha'-beta'/beta-beta/beta')lambda'=0, is the analogous condition in the reciprocal-symmetric (case III) form.

5. ELIMINATION BY DETERMINANTS. Solving R0, R1, R2 for xi (eta, zeta) by Cramer's rule gives
(1/alpha 1/beta 1/gamma) xi + (alpha 1/beta 1/gamma) x + ... = 0,
with bracket symbols as above. He expands the determinants:
- (alpha beta gamma) = alpha beta'-alpha' beta+alpha' gamma-alpha gamma'+beta gamma'-beta' gamma
- (1/alpha 1/beta 1/gamma) = 1/(alpha beta')-...
- the mixed one |1 1 1; beta 1/beta 1/gamma; beta' 1/beta' 1/gamma'| = beta/beta'-beta'/beta+beta'/gamma-beta/gamma'+1/(beta gamma')-1/(beta' gamma).

He factors the last as a combination of (beta-1/beta) and (beta'-1/beta'). The correct form is (beta-1/beta)(1/beta'-1/gamma')-(beta'-1/beta')(1/beta-1/gamma).

6. Bottom. A sketch of the quartic in the shape sqrt(x(...))+sqrt(y(...))+sqrt(z(...)) after substituting the eliminated forms. It involves (alpha'-1/alpha')x+(beta'-1/beta')y+(gamma'-1/gamma')z, i.e. the combination R2-type minus its reciprocal. That combination is what survives when alpha=beta=gamma=1-type degenerations are imposed. This part is left unfinished.
errors: The relation defining f: gamma b - beta gamma c - a + gamma d equals (gamma-beta)(gamma z+eta/beta), so with the written left side (beta-gamma)f one gets f = -(eta/beta+gamma z). This is a sign slip, harmless inside a square-root product.
In the square-root block the second factor is written (xi/alpha+eta/beta+gamma z); it must be (xi/alpha+eta/beta+zeta/gamma).

Combining sqrt(alpha/beta)*(first) with the second relation: to cancel sqrt(x xi) one must subtract, not add. The written signs only work up to the free choice of square-root signs. After squaring, the sign in front of 2 sqrt(alpha/beta)sqrt(AB) is opposite to the written one, again immaterial up to root signs.

The square-root relations sqrt((x+y+z)(xi+eta+zeta)) - sqrt(x xi) + sqrt(y eta) = 0 etc. are not consequences of R0-R2 in general. Note that by R0, (x+y+z)(xi+eta+zeta) = -(x+y+z)^2. They must rest on an unstated degenerate hypothesis, and the page gives no justification.

The marginal simplification of the lambda-compatibility condition, claimed to factor as (1-1/(beta gamma))(beta-gamma)(beta/gamma-2), does not check. Direct elimination gives beta^2/gamma-2beta+2gamma+1/gamma-(beta/gamma-2+gamma/beta+beta+1/beta), which does not vanish at beta*gamma=1 (e.g. beta=2). The working is visibly unfinished or erroneous.

The factorisation of the mixed determinant as transcribed, (beta-1/beta)(1/gamma-1/gamma')+(beta'-1/beta')(1/beta-1/gamma), is wrong. The correct identity is (beta-1/beta)(1/beta'-1/gamma')-(beta'-1/beta')(1/beta-1/gamma). This is possibly a transcription issue.
The condition derived here for case II (alpha=beta) is alpha' beta' = alpha'' beta''. The previous page's transcription has alpha' beta'' = alpha'' beta'; one of the two is a slip or misreading.

results.what: Use of the normal form of a plane quartic sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0, with six bitangents linked by x+y+z+xi+eta+zeta=0 and alpha x+...+xi/alpha+...=0 (two such), and 3-bit characteristics for the 63 half-periods / 28 bitangents
results.modern_name: Riemann's (Aronhold-system) normal form of the genus-3 quartic and its 28 bitangents via theta characteristics
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (lectures/posthumous 'Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen fuer den Fall p=3', Werke 1876); Aronhold 1864; Weber 1876

results.what: Elimination of xi, eta, zeta by Cramer's rule with 3x3 determinants (a b c) = |1 1 1; a b c; a' b' c'| and their expansion/factorisation

Degeneration analysis: conditions on the moduli (alpha,beta,gamma,alpha',...) such as alpha=beta with alpha'beta'=alpha''beta'' under which pairs of bitangents in a group coincide, with characteristic bookkeeping of the affected pairs
results.modern_name: Degenerations of plane quartics / boundary of moduli in Riemann/Aronhold coordinates (bitangent coincidences)
results.usually_credited_to: Weber (1876 monograph on p=3) and later work on degenerate quartics; unsure of exact precedence

results.what: Construction of new 'bitangent-type' products (eta+zeta)(beta y+gamma z), (y+z)(eta/beta+zeta/gamma), (y+zeta)(eta/beta+gamma z) by linear recombination in a special case, plus a pencil-parameter lambda condition
results.modern_name: Linear-algebraic identification of further bitangent pairs (Steiner complexes / syzygetic pairs) in a special configuration
results.usually_credited_to: Steiner, Hesse, Riemann, Weber (theory of the 28 bitangents)

deep.surprise_reason: This is working material in Riemann's own, already published framework for p=3 (quartic normal form, characteristics, 63 half-periods). The page explores special or degenerate parameter cases with partly unfinished and partly erroneous algebra. The detailed case analysis of degenerations is a modestly interesting unpublished detail, but contains no major result attributable to later authors.

transcription_corrections: Top line 'alpha=0' is probably 'alpha=1' (or equivalent), since x and xi drop out of the subsequent relations.
Third line should read alpha' x+beta' y+gamma' z+xi/alpha'+eta/beta'+zeta/gamma'=0 (not eta'/beta').
The labelled roots are sqrt((eta+zeta)(beta y+gamma z)) [a,b], sqrt((y+z)(eta/beta+zeta/gamma)) [c,d], sqrt((y+zeta)(eta/beta+gamma z)) [e,f], sqrt((eta+z)(beta y+zeta/gamma)).
'sqrt(x+eta+zeta)' in the first block is likely sqrt(xi+eta+zeta).
'(beta gamma)(lambda+1/lambda+beta+1/beta)' should be 'beta(lambda+1/lambda+beta+1/beta)' for the equation to hold with right side -(beta-gamma)^2/gamma.
In the square-root block, '(xi/alpha+eta/beta+gamma z)' should be '(xi/alpha+eta/beta+zeta/gamma)'.
'n gamma + ...' at the start of the right-margin line is probably '2 gamma' or '2(gamma-beta)'.
'(1/alpha 1/beta 1/gamma) eta + ...' at the start of the elimination line should be '... xi + ...' (solving for xi).
